First, we substitute $u=\sqrt{x}.$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,⟹\,2\text{d}u=\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\text{d}x.
$$

Since $u\to \infty $ when $x\to \infty ,$ the table for the limits of integration using the rule $u=\sqrt{x}$ is as follows:

| $x$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $\infty $ |

So, the integral in terms of the new variable $u$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{e}^{-\sqrt{2x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-\sqrt{2}u}\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we proceed by setting the upper bound equal to some parameter $a,$ integrating as usual, and then taking the limit as $a\to \infty .$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{e}^{-\sqrt{2x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{0}^{\infty }{e}^{-\sqrt{2}u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{\int }_{0}^{a}{e}^{-\sqrt{2}u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =2\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[-\frac{{e}^{-\sqrt{2}u}}{\sqrt{2}}]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot {lim}_{a\to \infty }{[{e}^{-\sqrt{2}u}]}_{0}^{a} \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\frac{1}{{e}^{\sqrt{2}a}}-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, recall the end behavior of the function $y=\frac{1}{{e}^{\sqrt{2}x}},$ shown in the graph below:

- ${lim}_{x\to -\infty }\frac{1}{{e}^{\sqrt{2}x}}=\infty $

- ${lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{1}{{e}^{\sqrt{2}x}}=0$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14037234/assets/5e9932629e5a201c2ada61157fdfa39351962a55116e2980157b1823907159f2.png)

Using this to evaluate our integral, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{\infty }\frac{{e}^{-\sqrt{2x}}}{\sqrt{x}}\,\text{d}x & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot ({lim}_{a\to \infty }\frac{1}{{e}^{\sqrt{2}a}}-1) \\  & =-\sqrt{2}\cdot (0-1) \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
